items.title: Top 5 Tech Stocks Built to Weather Higher Interest Rates
items.summary: These five tech stocks are built to weather higher rates with strong balance sheets, robust cash flow, and financial flexibility.

items.title: Is Cisco Stock Priced For Orders That Are Not Yet Revenue?
items.summary: Cisco Systems (CSCO) grew revenue more slowly over the last twelve months than any other company in its peer group. Yet it trades on almost the same earnings multiple as Dell Technologies, the fastest grower of the five. Trailing growth does not explain that price on its own. Cisco's last quarter grew 18%, well ahead of its 11.8% twelve-month figure. The rest of the case rests on AI networking orders that are running well ahead of the revenue Cisco has booked from them.

items.title: 2 Cybersecurity Stocks That Will Rule 2027
items.summary: As AI-related fears increase, cybersecurity stocks could be the heroes that businesses and investors need.

items.title: Can Palo Alto Networks' SASE Push Help It Challenge FTNT and ZS?
items.summary: PANW's SASE bookings surge 40% in fiscal 2026 as platform consolidation and rising AI traffic create opportunities to challenge FTNT and ZS.

items.title: Should You Buy Synopsys Stock While Its Cash Runs Far Ahead Of Its Profit?
items.summary: Synopsys (SNPS) sells the design software and the interface IP that chip makers need to get AI silicon built, and its stock has still gone backwards over the past year. At about $370 the shares sit at their 52-week low. Reported margins have fallen sharply over the past year. Free cash flow tells a different story, and the gap between cash and reported profit is the case worth arguing here.

items.title: The Ultimate Cyber Shield: CrowdStrike Rises Past $235
items.summary: CrowdStrike shares hit 52-week highs near $242 after strong Q2 results showed 25.6% revenue growth and 51% ARR expansion, as cybersecurity spending resists broader tech budget cuts.

items.title: What Does Fortinet (FTNT) Gain From Its New York Innovation Hub?
items.summary: Fortinet (NasdaqGS:FTNT) has opened a new company-owned Innovation Hub in New York City to expand its U.S. footprint. The New York facility includes advanced cybersecurity training labs, executive briefing spaces, and hands-on technology demonstration areas. The hub also introduces a dedicated Fortinet Cloud point of presence and energy-efficient infrastructure aligned with the group’s ESG priorities.
